messages.author: 82933c06b1097cc4
messages.subject: scantwo permutation took too long
parts:
Hi,
I'm recently running a qtl analysis on cluster, but the permutation took too long! After running for 4 days Iam still waiting for the permutation results? Am I doing something wrong?
Please find more details below:
set.seed(3131)
perm_scan2_Ben.em<-scantwo(mydata_ril_iso_calc,
pheno.col="Benzylbenzoate",model="normal",method="em",n.perm=1000,
n.cluster=1,addcovar=NULL,intcovar=NULL,weights=NULL,
clean.output=FALSE, clean.nmar=FALSE,clean.distance=FALSE,
incl.markers=TRUE, assumeCondIndep=FALSE,verbose=FALSE)

I requested 4 cores with four threads each at a memory of 10 gb each.
Thanks
Gill

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scantwo permutation took too long
parts:
Scantwo permutations take a long time, especially if you have many markers.

1000 permutations will take at least as 1000x as long as running scantwo once, and there can problems with running out of memory which will really slow things down.

If you can use method="hk", things will be much faster.

Also try the scantwopermhk() function, which works only for Haley-Knott regression, but was reorganized to try to speed things up.

I'd also recommend doing the permutations in smaller batches and then combining the results with c().

karl
